characters.mnemonic: Starts like the number 3, tethered by a line to a vertical pillar under a roof.
The base vowel "अ" reinforced with an extra parallel pillar.
An S-shaped serpent hanging by its head with a curled tail.
The short "इ" serpent wearing an eagle feather atop its roof.
A graceful numeral 3 suspended freely from the ceiling.
The vowel "उ" sprouting a long tail arching down.
An open doorway with a tilted latch under the roof: "E".
The letter "E" wearing an antenna plume flag: "Ai".
Letter "Aa" with a single flag rising above the roof: "O".
Letter "Aa" crowned with two flying flags: "Au".
A vertical central trunk with a round leaf on the left and a falling leaf on the right.
Resembles "ra" and "va" joining together under one shared roof.
A walking cane with a looped handle standing next to a tall flagpole.
A stacked double-bowl resting against a tall column.
The serpentine "ड" accompanied by a nasal dot beside its curve: "Nga".
A teacup handle attached to a supportive right wall.
An umbrella handle looping under rain clouds: "Chha" for Chhatri.
A ladle scooping water (Jal) anchored to a firm pillar.
An "इ"-shaped flag flapping on a flagpole: "Jha" for Jhandaa.
A backwards crescent moon tethered to a pillar: palatal "Nya".
A hanging basket with a wide open front: retroflex "Ṭa" for Tamatar (tomato).
A circular bell hanging under the roof: aspirated retroflex "Ṭha".
An S-shaped hourglass drum (Damru) suspended from the roof: "Ḍa".
A covered bowl with a lid knob inside: voiced aspirate "Ḍha" for Dhakkan (lid).
A U-shaped magnet standing right beside a tall pillar: retroflex nasal "Ṇa".
An arching sword (Talwar) hanging from a strong pillar.
A looped pitcher resting beside a pillar: aspirated dental "Tha".
A dental stop "Da" curving down with a hanging tail for Dawa (medicine).
A curled archer's bow (Dhanush) anchored to a pillar: "Dha".
A water tap (Nal) flowing horizontally into a pipe pillar.
A floating kite (Patang) string secured to a post.
The letter "प" sprouting an arching spray of fruits (Phal).
A round belly with a belt slash tied to a pillar: "Ba" for Bakri (goat).
The letter "म" adorned with an open upper loop: voiced aspirate "Bha".
A fish (Machhli) swimming into an upright post under a roof.
A sacred fire vessel without the head loop: palatal semivowel "Ya".
A royal chariot (Rath) wheel with a trailing banner.
A double-curved spinning top (Lattoo) anchored to a pillar: "La".
A round belly loop on a pillar without any internal slash: "Va" for Van (forest).
A royal conch shell (Shankh) resting beside a temple pillar: "Sha".
Letter "Pa" crossed with a diagonal sword slash: retroflex sibilant "Ṣa".
A serpent coiled on the left tethered to a solid right pillar.
An elephant's trunk (Haathi) playfully curving in the air.
The Aa-ki-matra stands beside a consonant (e.g. क + ा = का "kaa").
Halant cuts off the inherent "a" sound, producing pure consonants and conjuncts (e.g. क् = k).
